text: Term starts. Year nine again, thirty-one kids. Kofi starts at the secondary school across town, not mine. He insisted. I understand, but it stings a little.
Allotment handover. Plot 14, overgrown with brambles. Desmond from plot 12 lent me a scythe and a lot of advice I didn't ask for.
Ma's blood pressure is high again. The GP wants her on new tablets. She says she feels fine. She always feels fine.
Choir rehearsal. We're learning the Fauré for the spring concert. The tenors are a disaster and I am one of the tenors.
Kofi came home quiet. Wouldn't say why. Ate dinner in his room. Abena thinks it's just settling in.
Cleared half the brambles. Found an old rhubarb crown under there. Desmond says it's thirty years old. Took it as a sign.
Boiler broke. Quote for a new one is more than we have in savings. Spent the night doing sums with Abena. We'll have to use the credit card.
Kofi finally talked. Some boys in his class have been calling him names about his accent. He made me promise not to go to the school. I promised. I'm furious.
Marked sixty essays this weekend. My eyes have stopped working. Missed choir.
Ma fainted at church. Ambulance, A&E, a long night on plastic chairs. They kept her in to adjust the tablets.
Ma's home. The doctor said the new dose was too strong. She's annoyed at the fuss. I'm just relieved.
Broke my promise and emailed Kofi's form tutor, Ms. Varga, very carefully. She called back within an hour and was kind. She'd noticed something already.
Planted garlic and broad beans on the cleared half of the plot. Desmond nodded, which I think is high praise.
Inspection announced for next month. The staffroom went silent. Head says not to panic, which made everyone panic.
Kofi told me Ms. Varga moved him to a different group and the name-calling has mostly stopped. He wasn't angry I'd emailed. He said 'thanks, Dad' at the door and ran off.
Paid off the first chunk of the boiler debt. Still a long way to go but the number is going the right direction.
Choir: the tenors have improved. Slightly. The conductor, Mrs. Ansah, said 'less like a lorry reversing'. We'll take it.
Inspection week. Three lessons observed. One went brilliantly, one fine, one where the projector died and a boy was sick. Survived.
Inspection result: 'good'. The head bought cakes. I slept eleven hours.
Ma's sixtieth-ish birthday (she won't confirm the number). Whole family at ours. Kofi played guitar for her and she cried.
Frost killed the broad beans. Desmond said he'd told me to fleece them. He had.
Abena and I had a real argument about money. She wants to cancel the holiday; I want one thing to look forward to. We both said things we didn't mean.
Made up with Abena. We agreed on a cheap week at her sister's by the coast instead. Fair.
Desmond's wife passed away. He wasn't at the allotment for a week. I left soup on his doorstep and watered his seedlings.
Kofi got a part in the school play. A small one, three lines. He practises them in the shower so loudly the neighbours know them too.
Ma's check-up: blood pressure finally normal on the new tablets. The GP was pleased. Ma said 'I told you I was fine'.
Desmond back on his plot today. We didn't talk about his wife. He showed me how to stake tomatoes. That was the conversation.
Spring concert. The Fauré went well and the tenors held together. Abena and Ma in the second row. Proudest I've felt in ages.
Exhausted. Report writing season. Two hundred reports, each one a little lie of encouragement.
Kofi's play. He said his three lines perfectly and then took a bow nobody asked for. Ma whooped.
First harvest: rhubarb from the thirty-year-old crown. Made a crumble. Took half to Desmond.
Credit card cleared! The boiler is finally ours. Celebrated with fish and chips.
Week at the coast with Abena's family. Rained four days out of seven. Played cards, ate too much, laughed a lot.
Ma had a dizzy spell. Probably the heat, the doctor said. Probably. I'm checking on her every day.
Kofi wants to move to my school for sixth form. Said the other one was 'fine but not mine'. I didn't say anything clever. I just grinned.
Desmond gave me his old greenhouse. Says he's getting too old to use it. I think he wanted me to have something of his.
